title: Derivation DAG from <> through Pre-Genesis, Genesis, L1 emergence, L1-to-L2 and the Hilbert lift to finite quantum mechanics
scope: Extraction from repository sources on main at the source commit, plus nodes for proposals that are open as draft pull requests. The DAG records what each source states and where a derivation is absent. It does not extend any derivation and promotes no status.

status_legend.ADMITTED_PRIMITIVE: posited as an input of the programme, not derived
status_legend.DEFINITION: a definition in the cited source
status_legend.PROVED_PROSE: a prose proof in the cited source; no Lean artifact
status_legend.PROVED_LEAN: a named Lean declaration exists in the checkout and the source cites it; elaboration was not re-run here
status_legend.COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED: an exact finite computation or Rust/Python control; not a proof for the general statement
status_legend.CONDITIONAL: holds under a stated hypothesis that the source does not discharge
status_legend.IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION: structure supplied from outside the derivation and named as such
status_legend.OPEN: unproved, unwritten, or a proposal whose pull request is not merged
status_legend.SOURCE_RECORD: a step the cited source records, or a fence label from a TFQ source slice; the DAG assigns it no derivation status

edge_semantics: A route requires all of its inputs and yields its output.
Routes with the same output are alternatives.
GAP_NO_DERIVATION marks a join that the sources assert but do not derive; it carries no source.
CONDITIONAL_ON_IMPORT marks a join that holds once the named imported structure is supplied.
see_also on a node lists nodes from other segments that cover the same question under a different source.
RECORD_PARENT marks the TFQ tree link from a record to its parent record; it asserts reading order, not a derivation.
non_discharge_notes: <> is an inert inscription in the Pre-Genesis and Genesis papers. The admitted root Difference joined with Structure is defined elsewhere. No source derives the second from the first, and the DAG keeps them as two nodes joined by a gap.
No source read derives the l1 sector weights from the Phi1 and Gamma2 residual. Weights enter as declared mass.

The lift from L1 to a Hilbert space imports a complex field, U(1) phases, an inner product, orthogonal additivity, independent Haar phases and linear isometric dynamics. Only the finite matrix algebra over Gaussian integers is recovered.
Nodes tagged proposed-pr-open are proposals in draft pull requests. They are not proved on main.
A PROVED_LEAN status means a named declaration exists and a source cites it. Receipts, hashes and ledger flags were not treated as proof.

nodes.statement: The replies to the fixed Prompt 11 give at least two admissible continuations of <>: Trial 1 proposed no successor (quiescence) and Trial 2 proposed <> again under an added repetition rule, so |Adm(P_1)| ≥ 2 for that one prompt. The two replies rest on different proposed assumptions, so they show that the prompt did not prescribe a continuation, not that one fixed transition system has two successors. Primitive Difference plus the prompt does not determine a unique S_1; selecting a canonical next stage needs declared operations and a selection rule, such as a minimality order, a cost functional, a deterministic tie-breaker or retention of every tied minimal branch.

nodes.statement: To tell 'the inscription remains' from 'a second occurrence has been produced', a regime needs at least two stages or positions, an identity criterion across them, a copying or persistence rule and a stable alphabet: repetition is succession plus retained identity. Trial 2's proposed step <> → <> therefore already carries structure, the self-loop id_<> : <> → <>, and is not a free primitive. The first generated operation may then be identity, persistence or reproduction rather than a new payload such as <a>. The source labels this an analysis of what the word 'repeat' presupposes, not a proof.
nodes.bottleneck: Treat a proposed repetition of <> as requiring declared positions, a cross-position identity criterion, a persistence rule and a stable alphabet, and record a self-loop as added structure, not as the absence of a step.

nodes.source_status: TFQ record_status SOURCE_RECORD (source slice pregenesis_to_wdp)
nodes.statement: For Prompt 15 the full replay offered four extensions that would separate <a> from <ab> (declarative distinctness, conditional deletion, insertion and substitution), with no new glyphs and no counting, and said none was unique. Prompt 18 then defined a one-step extension as one that adds exactly one primitive capability, and the reply refused all four as one-step; the failure-mode chapter records that each needed several undeclared capabilities, such as branching, matching and rewriting. The refusal ties to the spine of relations that the Trial 2 failures had pulled apart, mention → supply → designation → admission → retention → internal operation, and the analysis that draws it adds that not every arrow has yet been defined. In the declared two-flag admission model of Paper000.lean no single act (datum, form or instance) separates from the empty state, while form then instance does.
nodes.bottleneck: Count the capabilities an extension adds against the six-operation spine, refuse to label it one-step when it adds more than one, and leave the undefined arrows of the spine undefined.

nodes.source_status: TFQ record_status DEFINITION (source slice pregenesis_to_wdp)
nodes.statement: The PFP non-conflation law keeps three acts apart. Repair inside a frozen context is a same-level adjustment within the declared repair gauge W = im d₀ that changes slot values without altering the carrier set or the cochain dimension. Extending the representation (Λₙ) adjoins carrier elements, cochain dimensions or relations after same-level repair is exhausted, under the 12 extension audit conditions. Promoting evidence or authorizing action (Ω) moves an object across the authority firewall, and model output, packet admission, local replay and zero residuals never authorize external actions.
nodes.bottleneck: Type every PFP act as repair, extend or promote, and refuse any route that turns a zero residual, a replay or an admission into an authorization.

nodes.source_status: TFQ record_status DEFINITION (source slice pregenesis_to_wdp)
nodes.statement: When a packet family declares a cochain representation C⁰ → C¹ → C² with maps d₀ and d₁, the discrepancy of a candidate 1-cochain c is measured by the boundary defect Φ₁ = ‖[c]‖ in C¹/im d₀ (the quotient infimum of ‖c − d₀a‖ over 0-cochains a), the cycle defect Γ₂ = ‖d₁c‖ in C², and the total residual Ξ = Φ₁ + Γ₂; a candidate is accepted exactly when Ξ = 0 over the declared observer. Because d₁d₀ = 0, Φ₁ = 0 forces Γ₂ = 0, so Ξ = 0 exactly when Φ₁ = 0. Worked example: on the oriented triangle 0 → 1 → 2 → 0 with one declared face, c = (1, 1, 1) gives Φ₁ = 3 and Γ₂ = 3, so Ξ = 6, while c = (1, 1, −2) = d₀(0, 1, 2) gives Φ₁ = Γ₂ = Ξ = 0.
nodes.bottleneck: Compute Φ₁ as the exact quotient infimum and Γ₂ under the declared face map with exact rationals, report both, and accept only at Ξ = 0.

nodes.source_status: 000_oepregen grammar/pre_genesis.ebnf lines 1-37; 30 conformance cases PG_001-PG_030
nodes.statement: The Pre-Genesis host grammar declares the inscription alphabet {<, >, a, b} and three public starts: ground_token (exactly <>), inscription (one balanced, non-nested bracketed inscription) and pre_genesis_regime (zero or more inscriptions between braces, where {} is host list notation and not the empty word). It keeps four states apart: absent input, the empty word, the literal token <> and the ground carrier that S(0) adopts. It has no event productions: the first event, supply(<>), is the Genesis boundary, and parsing a word admits no carrier, transition or observational operation.
imported_structure: Declared host grammar pre_genesis.ebnf, a later host notation not tested by the model trials (assumption)
nodes.bottleneck: A grammar verdict is a syntax check of host notation; it assigns no semantics to <> and does not decide whether an inscription is admitted.

nodes.source_status: 000_oepregen 03_results_and_arguments.md section 1 (statement 1, true by definition)
nodes.statement: If a regime's transition relation is empty, no state has a successor; that is the definition of an empty relation and needs no experiment. All three replies to Prompt 11 said no continuation is forced, so a move from <> to <a> has to come from outside: a caller supplies it, or a rule is added.

nodes.source_status: 000_genesis_19l57g1 paper.md section 4 definition; v1 Formalization B; 000_oepregen rewriting Definition 2.3
nodes.statement: Relative to the family O_n of internal observations available at stage n, x ≈ₙ y holds exactly when o(x) = o(y) for every o in O_n, with equality taken in each observation's codomain. If O_n is empty, every pair is equivalent vacuously, so with no observations <a> ≈ₙ <ab>. This is regime-relative equivalence: it does not make the strings equal and does not install an equality operator inside the regime.
imported_structure: A declared carrier of inscriptions and a declared family O_n of observations on it (assumption)
nodes.bottleneck: The relation depends on the declared O_n and compares observation values in the metatheory; it is not literal string equality and does not say which observations a regime should have.

nodes.source_status: 000_oepregen 03_results_and_arguments.md section 2 (statement 2, holds under one convention); v1 Derivation 3
nodes.statement: Write P for the presented inscriptions and O for the internal observations. Supplying <a> after <> changes P from {<>} to {<a>} and leaves O_1 = O_0 = ∅, so no new internal distinction is available. With q : P → N sending an inscription to the distinctions the regime has, x ≠ y in P can hold while q(x) = q(y) in N, so a new presentation does not imply a new internal class, and in the other direction q(x) = q(y) does not imply x = y. Under the opaque convention <a> is a new presentation state in the same internal class as <>; the statement holds under that convention only.
imported_structure: Opaque identity convention: a state is what the regime can tell apart, so internal identity is the quotient by ≈ₙ (assumption)
nodes.bottleneck: Under the exact-inscription convention <a> is a new state; the statement concerns discriminating power, not meaning, since a regime can gain a syntactic distinction such as empty versus nonempty payload without assigning a a referent.

nodes.source_status: v1 Red round item 1 (conditional verdict); 000_oepregen 03_results_and_arguments.md section 2 and 02_trial_record.md Prompt 12
nodes.statement: Whether <a> supplied after <> is a new state depends on an identity convention that no prompt had declared. Under the opaque convention a state is what the regime can tell apart, and with O empty <> and <a> are not told apart; under the exact-inscription convention a state is the inscription itself, the strings differ, and the regime has one more syntactic state. Trials 1 and 2 answered under the first convention and the full replay under the second, calling <a> a new state. The analysis keeps both branches and records the effect as undecidable until one convention is declared.
imported_structure: A declared identity convention, opaque or exact-inscription, chosen by the host (assumption)
nodes.bottleneck: Records that the answer is relative to the convention; it does not choose one, and the three replies are behaviour of one unrecorded model, not evidence for either convention.

nodes.source_status: v1 section 3 Formalization A (declared UNDECIDABLE status) beside Formalization B; 04_named_failure_modes.md premature relation
nodes.statement: Asked whether the regime distinguishes <a> and <ab>, identifies them or cannot decide, Trial 1 answered that the current regime identifies them; the analysis corrects this, since the absence of a distinguishing rule does not imply identification. Formalization A: with no equality, equivalence or observation relation declared, neither <a> = <ab> nor <a> ≠ <ab> is internally derivable, and status(<a>, <ab>) = UNDECIDABLE. Formalization B is the separate definition ≈ₙ, under which an empty O_n gives <a> ≈ₙ <ab> vacuously. The reply 'identifies them' imported an identification relation unless B had been declared first, and the failure-mode chapter names it premature relation.

nodes.source_status: 000_oepregen 03_results_and_arguments.md section 5 (statement 5, argument with proof); 000_genesis_19l57g1 paper.md Proposition 1; Lean Paper000.separation_not_on_quotient
nodes.statement: Suppose an external task requires <a> and <ab> to differ while the current regime has <a> ≈ₙ <ab>. Every operation f on the quotient S_n/≈ₙ gives f([<a>]) = f([<ab>]), so no operation on the current quotient answers the task on every input, and a refinement adding at least one observation o with o(<a>) ≠ o(<ab>) is forced; the analysis gives this as an argument with proof. The lift is not unique: under a supplied string decoder, 'payload has more than one position' and 'payload contains b' both separate <a> from <ab> but disagree on <aa> (true and false), and full inscription identity also separates the pair while carrying more than one bit. A canonical tower therefore needs a declared minimality or initiality policy, such as fewest new predicates, minimum description length, maximal preservation of old equivalences, a free or initial completion, or retention of every tied minimum branch.
imported_structure: Supplied string decoder for the payloads of <a>, <ab> and <aa>, used only by the non-uniqueness example (assumption)
nodes.bottleneck: The Lean declarations cover the quotient barrier; the non-uniqueness of the lift rests on the two-predicate example, and no selection policy, fixed ladder of quotients or minimal multiplicity lift is derived.

nodes.source_status: 000_oepregen 03_results_and_arguments.md section 6 (statement 6, theorem with proof); v1 Derivation 4; Lean Paper000.insufficient_history_view
nodes.statement: Let H be the possible histories, σ(h) the state that history h produces and π(h) the part of h an auditor sees, for example only the last turn. If π(h₁) = π(h₂) but σ(h₁) ≠ σ(h₂), no auditor A that sees only π reports σ(h) for every h, because A(π(h₁)) = A(π(h₂)) would give σ(h₁) = σ(h₂). The trial failures motivate the theorem: the blind auditor flagged the licensed words 'We' (Trial 1) and 'rule' (Trial 2) as imports, so an audit needs two levels; in Trial 2, Prompt 14's false attribution was answered without objection, so claim provenance is a check separate from claim correctness, Result 15 lost the state, saying the regime contains only <> after <a> had been supplied; and the two-level auditor, shown only that turn, answered None. State certification therefore needs replay information that separates the relevant histories, and on a declared finite population a summary on which σ is constant per fiber of the view can stand in for the raw history.
nodes.bottleneck: The trial contrasts motivate the theorem and do not instantiate it: the truncated window and the full replay received different inputs, so they are not a checked pair with equal auditor views; raw history retention is a provenance policy, and task-sufficient reconstruction is the mathematical requirement.

nodes.source_status: v1 Derivation 5 (clean theorem target, no proof); 000_oepregen 03_results_and_arguments.md section 7 (statement 7)
nodes.statement: A trace that starts from a declared context s′ and takes steps valid relative to s′ need not be valid relative to the actual replayed state s ≠ s′: ValidTrace(τ | s′) does not imply ValidTrace(τ | s). Trial 2's Result 15 is the example, with internally consistent reasoning from the stale premise s′ = {<>} after Prompt 12 had designated <a> as current. A sound execution contract therefore accepts a context binding C(s′) only when s′ = Replay(H). The analysis calls this a clean theorem target and gives no proof. The Prompt 17 contrast fits it: a truncated window answered Verified and the full replay Retracted, each right for the history it received, which the appended analysis calls an information boundary rather than a reasoning failure.
nodes.bottleneck: A target statement and verifier requirement with no proof and no declared trace semantics; the replay certifiers listed check a claimed Genesis regime against its event history and do not define ValidTrace.

nodes.source_status: recorded requirement: 000_oepregen 02_trial_record.md Prompts 18 and 19; curriculum Lesson 8; v1 Trial 2 main result
nodes.statement: Given the corrected state, the full replay answered that the task of making <a> and <ab> internally distinguishable cannot be evaluated until <ab> is brought into the regime. The first addition can supply <ab> as data or write it into a rule pattern; the two are equally minimal and neither is uniquely forced. After Prompt 19 admitted <ab> beside <a> with no comparison, counting or matching, nothing in the regime reacts to them differently, so admission alone distinguishes nothing and no unique continuation is dictated. The requirement recorded is an order: the regime must admit inscriptions, retain them across turns and replay the current state before a separation task on them can be posed.
nodes.bottleneck: A recorded requirement drawn from model replies that no host checker evaluated; the two-flag Lean and Python models encode admission acts and separation by declaration and do not choose a first addition.

nodes.source_status: genesis_source.txt section 2 [declared metatheory]; Bridge.lean admission-order theorems
nodes.statement: The sealed manuscript declares two levels. The metatheory holds presentation tokens (strings), event sequences, indices, finite data structures and arithmetic; the object language holds only what a regime admits. Token glyphs, component counts, order, concatenation, multiplicity, substring structure, matching and string equality live in the metatheory unless an admitted judgment internalizes a distinction. Presentation identity (token equality) is metatheory only, internal identity is the datum index, and no semantic interpretation is ever assigned.
imported_structure: Declared two-level metatheory/object-language split of genesis_source.txt section 2 (assumption)
nodes.bottleneck: A declared split, not a theorem: the Lean model has no tokens by construction, so token-blindness is structural there and is checked in Python and Rust by renaming tests; admission order is visible to the token-aware metatheory and erased at the object level.

nodes.source_status: paper.md section 6 and genesis_source.txt section 3.8 [definition]; Minimality.lean Iso
nodes.statement: A regime isomorphism is a pair of bijections on datum and form indices that preserves form arities, ordered instance arguments, uniform-rule membership and the separation requirements read as unordered pairs; mapped requirement endpoints are sorted before comparison, and presentation tokens are erased first. Because requirements are unordered, exchanging the endpoints of a requirement can identify two responses; a relation preserving directed requirements would be a different convention. The Lean structure Iso states these fields over the admitted index ranges, and sortPair is shown to equal (min, max) and to be symmetric.
imported_structure: Declared isomorphism convention with unordered requirement pairs, genesis_source.txt section 3.8 (assumption)
nodes.bottleneck: The convention is declared: Iso is a membership relation, so it also identifies list representations such as [p] and [p, p], and an isomorphism preserving directed requirements would give different tie classes.

nodes.source_status: genesis_source.txt section 4 [theorem] plus a [definition] for no forced successor; Inertia.lean, Bridge.lean
nodes.statement: At Challenge 0 the only object-language inscription is the opaque whole <>. In the token-erased Lean model nothing is derivable at genesis (genesis_underivable), and nothing is derivable in any regime with no instances and no rules (underivable_of_empty); the Challenge 0 computation records zero contexts and an empty derivable set in both readings. That no successor is internally forced is a property of the declared grammar, whose only state changes are external-event-indexed admissions, not a theorem about a forcing predicate. In the token-aware model a history whose datum admissions all carry one token leaves at most one admitted datum (single_token_carrier_bound), so a state with two data needs the admission of a second, different token (second_token_required).
nodes.bottleneck: No forcing predicate is defined, so no forced successor is a model-scoped definition and not a theorem, and nothing here excludes a successor in an extension of the language; supply_no_op itself is recorded under TFQ-0379.

nodes.source_status: genesis_source.txt sections 3.3-3.5 and paper.md section 6 [definition]; Basic.lean
nodes.statement: A context is an admitted form with a slot tuple of its arity in which every filled slot names an admitted datum and at least one slot is a hole; plugging a datum fills every hole with that same datum. Derivability is membership in the admitted instances or coverage by a uniform all-tuples rule, and no other inference exists. The profile of a datum is the set of well-formed contexts whose plugging is derivable. Two data are collapsed when their profiles are equal and separable when some well-formed context is derivable for one and not the other; that is the declared sense used for every separation requirement.
imported_structure: Declared derivability: admitted-instance membership or a uniform all-tuples rule, with no other inference (assumption)
nodes.bottleneck: These are declared definitions: separability means a difference in positive derivability only, and an imposed requirement records a demand for separation without making it hold.

nodes.source_status: genesis_source.txt section 5 and paper.md section 6 [theorem]; Inertia.lean collapsed_of_no_insts
nodes.statement: With no admitted instances, the derivability of a plugged context depends only on its form, so every pair of data is observationally collapsed (collapsed_of_no_insts). Uniform rules do not change this: a ruled form makes every plugging derivable alike. Retaining another datum alone therefore need not increase expressive power.
nodes.bottleneck: The statement covers instance-free regimes only; once an instance is admitted collapse is decided by the profiles, and a later uniform rule can again erase a separation (TFQ-0385).

nodes.source_status: genesis_source.txt section 6 [theorem] and [counterexample]; Inertia.lean
nodes.statement: At Challenge 2 both <a> and <ab> are supplied and retained, so reading L admits (<a>, <ab>) and reading F admits (<>, <a>, <ab>). In both readings every admitted pair is observationally collapsed (R2L_collapsed, R2F_collapsed): two externally distinct inscriptions remain internally indistinguishable. The countermodel admission_without_expressive_increase admits a fresh datum, a real state change, while the pair stays collapsed, a counterexample to the claim that a new external inscription necessarily increases internal expressive power. The recorded Challenge 0-3 histories replay exactly to the Challenge 3 regimes R2L and R2F (historyL_replays, historyF_replays).
nodes.bottleneck: Admission changed only the metatheoretic datum count and the replayable history; glyph identity, component count, order and substring structure stay internally unavailable, and the readings stay unselected (TFQ-0380).

nodes.source_status: paper.md section 6 counting corollary (ledger WDP-P000-015); companion Paper.lean contextWords theorems
nodes.statement: For a regime with n admitted data, a form of arity a has (n+1)^a − n^a well-formed contexts: each slot is a hole or one of n data, less the n^a hole-free tuples, so |Ctx(R)| = Σ_f ((n+1)^{a_f} − n^{a_f}), with distinct form identifiers kept disjoint even when their arities coincide. The companion Lean module establishes the per-form count for the recursive word enumeration (contextWords_length), characterizes its members as exactly the well-formed words of that length containing a hole (contextWords_mem), and shows the enumeration has no repetitions (contextWords_nodup). The standalone replay checks the formula against the frozen Python enumeration in 35 cases (n from 0 to 4, arity 1 to 7), and Python and Rust enumerate the contexts independently.
nodes.bottleneck: The Lean statement is a companion result for the slot words of one form; the sum over forms is the written corollary of ledger row WDP-P000-015, which attributes it to no compiled source theorem, and large arities make profile enumeration expensive.

nodes.source_status: genesis_source.txt section 3 membership extensionality [theorem]; Ext.lean
nodes.statement: Python's admitted collections are sets while Lean's are deduplicated lists. Under RegimeExt (equal datum counts and form tables, and membership-equal instance, rule and requirement collections) every stated observable transports: derivability, context well-formedness, collapse, separability, item and delta application, and response validity (derivable_ext through validResponse_ext). Two list representations of the same admitted sets therefore agree on each of those observables.
nodes.bottleneck: Lean-to-Lean only: equal datum counts and equal indexed form tables stay premises, that every exported claim factors through these observables is not asserted, and executable comparisons with Python and Rust have their own input populations.

nodes.source_status: genesis_source.txt sections 3.6-3.7 and paper.md section 7 [definition]; Basic.lean, Minimality.lean aritySum
nodes.statement: A response (delta) is an ordered finite list of NewDatum, NewForm(arity), NewInst(form, args) and NewRuleAll(form) items applied in order; an instance may name a form added earlier in the same list, and the reverse order is an ill-formed admission. The declared costs are mu1 = item count and mu2 = (item count, sum of new-form arities) compared lexicographically, where the sum counts every NewForm item, including distinct forms of equal arity. A valid response to Separate(i, j) applies, separates the target, and keeps every previously imposed requirement separated, because requirements are persistent constraints.
imported_structure: Declared item grammar and cost measures mu1 and mu2, genesis_source.txt sections 3.6-3.7 (assumption)
nodes.bottleneck: Both measures and the item grammar are declared, not derived; bundling a form and an instance into one primitive would change every cost, and the enumerator's canonical item order makes a delta a multiset only up to that convention.

nodes.source_status: genesis_source.txt section 7.1 and question 5 [theorem]; Quot.lean
nodes.statement: Challenge 3 requires <a> and <ab> to be internally separable in the declared sense of positive derivability. Instantiating R2L_collapsed and R2F_collapsed, the current regime fails this: no witness context exists. The quotient barrier then applies: every function out of a quotient by a relation is constant on related elements (quotient_barrier, quot_barrier), and on the collapse classes of R2L any operation takes equal values on data 0 and 1 (barrier_R2L). An operation defined only on the current abstraction therefore cannot recover the required distinction, and a response has to change the regime.
nodes.bottleneck: The barrier concerns operations defined on the given quotient; it puts no bound on what an admitted augmentation of the regime can separate, which is the subject of the cost results (TFQ-0381).

nodes.source_status: genesis_source.txt section 7.3 [theorem, reading L]; Minimality.lean mu1_minimum_not_unique
nodes.statement: Under mu1 in reading L the minimum corrective augmentation is not unique. The unary mark deltaU0 and the binary link deltaBL are both valid two-item responses to Challenge 3 on R2L, no response of at most one item is valid, and their results U0 and BL are non-isomorphic because form arity is an isomorphism invariant (mu1_minimum_not_unique, U0_not_iso_BL). The theorem is stated over R2L only.
imported_structure: Declared item grammar, measure mu1 and the implemented isomorphism relation (assumption)
nodes.bottleneck: Reading L only: reading-F non-uniqueness is the bounded engine enumeration of five classes (TFQ-0442), and under mu2 the minimum is unique up to isomorphism (TFQ-0382).

nodes.source_status: genesis_source.txt section 7.3 [theorem, reading L] (CL-3-INFINITE-TIES); Minimality.lean markK family
nodes.statement: For every arity k ≥ 1 the k-ary mark, one k-ary form and one instance (1, ..., 1), is a valid two-item response to Challenge 3 on R2L (deltaK_valid, deltaK_length), since the all-hole context separates the two required data. Distinct arities give non-isomorphic results because an isomorphism preserves form arity (markK_pairwise_noniso), so the mu1 tie class in reading L is countably infinite. A concrete enumeration is therefore complete only relative to an arity bound, and the arity-at-most-two census is one slice of this family.
imported_structure: Declared item grammar, measure mu1 and the implemented isomorphism relation (assumption)
nodes.bottleneck: Stated over R2L only: no reading-F analogue of the k-ary family is formalized, and the family leaves the mu2 minimum (2, 1) unique up to isomorphism.

nodes.source_status: genesis_source.txt section 7.3 [bounded theorem] engine enumeration at (2,2); reproduce.py minimum census
nodes.statement: Within the declared bounds of at most two items and form arity at most two, exhaustive enumeration under mu1, cross-checked against the unpruned space, finds at (2,2) six valid deltas in three isomorphism classes for reading L (unary mark, binary link, binary self-loop) and ten valid deltas in five classes for reading F. Reading F's two extra classes link to and from the never-required genesis datum, and they are non-isomorphic to each other because the bijection must preserve the requirement pair. Under mu2 each reading has two minimal deltas in one class. The standalone replay reproduces all four counts.

nodes.bottleneck: A bounded census: it is the max_arity = 2 slice of the infinite mu1 tie family of reading L (TFQ-0441), and no reading-F Lean non-uniqueness statement exists.

nodes.source_status: genesis_source.txt sections 3.9-3.10 and 8.1 [declared metatheory]
nodes.statement: After Challenge 3 the challenge source is a pair of declared policies. The pair-separation closure policy reissues the admitted separation requirement pattern on collapsed pairs, one challenge branch per automorphism orbit of collapsed pairs, or nothing at the fixpoint where every pair is separated; it reads only profile equality and automorphism structure, supplies no data and imports no new goal kind. At that fixpoint the external continuation policy supplies and admits one fresh opaque token, and runs with this policy disabled are the closed-system baseline. Round 1 of every tree answers the externally imposed Challenge 3 requirement, and later separation rounds answer the closure policy.
imported_structure: Declared pair-separation closure policy and external continuation policy, genesis_source.txt sections 3.9-3.10 (assumption)
nodes.bottleneck: A collapsed pair is not an active obstruction by itself; the declared policy makes it one, its orbit-representative selection is also declared, and choosing it among conceivable policies is a declared-metatheory judgment, not a derived transition.

nodes.source_status: genesis_source.txt section 8.2 [counterexample] and relation-level [theorem] (R7); TransitionTransport.lean
nodes.statement: Raw least-pair selection is not isomorphism-equivariant. On the regression regime (four data, one unary form, instances on data 2 and 3) both the regime and its renaming by the double transposition 0↔2, 1↔3 collapse the pair (0, 1), yet the renaming carries (0, 1) to (2, 3) (least_pair_selection_not_congruent); that the two same-index choices give non-isomorphic children is a computational test. The repair branches once per automorphism orbit of collapsed pairs. Under datum renamings with forms fixed, the selection-free transition relation over every collapsed pair and every valid response transports (transStep_rename_fwd, transStep_image_total), and valid-response counts over caller-supplied candidate lists transport (validCount_rename).
nodes.bottleneck: The congruence is relation-level with forms fixed; conversion to equal canonical-key class sets, form-bijection transport and minimum-family transport stay computational with CL-ISO-SOUND, and no exported run reached a state with more than one orbit.

nodes.source_status: genesis_source.txt section 8.2 [theorem] (CL-PROGRESS); Progress.lean mark_progress
nodes.statement: On any well-formed regime whose imposed requirements are all separated, for any two distinct admitted data i and j, the two-item delta of one fresh unary form and one instance of it at datum j is a valid response to Separate(i, j) and keeps every imposed requirement separated (mark_progress). Derivability of instances of the old forms is unchanged by this extension, so old witnesses survive (derivable_extend). The standalone replay checks fresh-mark preservation for 3,996 targets across 1,436 regimes, and no terminal_no_response node occurs in any exported run.
nodes.bottleneck: This is response existence for a supplied demand only; it does not establish autonomous demand generation or an unbounded tower, and the preserved conjunct ranges over the requirement store, not over all separable pairs.

nodes.source_status: genesis_source.txt section 8.3 [theorem] (R1-R4) with CL-PRUNE-STRUCTURAL [bounded theorem]; Progress, RuleBridge, Mention .lean
nodes.statement: A separation witness never inhabits a uniformly ruled form, so shrinking the final rule set preserves every separation (separable_of_subrules). With the item-level bridge applyDelta_dropRules, a delta containing a uniform-rule item is never minimal: dropping its rule items leaves a valid, strictly shorter delta with the same new-form arity sum (rule_item_never_minimal). The mention lemma shows that appending instances that mention neither datum of a pair leaves that pair's collapse unchanged (collapsed_append_unmentioning), and under the well-formedness conjuncts a fresh unreferenced datum or form leaves the collapse of every existing pair unchanged (collapsed_fresh_datum, collapsed_fresh_form).
nodes.bottleneck: The three irrelevance inputs and the rule bridge are theorems, but the enclosing claim that the pruned cost-2 enumeration contains every minimum (CL-PRUNE-STRUCTURAL) stays a bounded theorem on computational evidence over the declared grammar slice.

nodes.source_status: genesis_source.txt question 8 and register row R6 [theorem]; CountTransport.lean, IsoCollapse.lean, FormTransport.lean
nodes.statement: Observational collapse is invariant under a renaming of datum indices with forms fixed: the renamed regime collapses the renamed pair exactly when the original regime collapses the original pair (collapsed_rename). For any caller-supplied candidate pair list with deciders that track collapse, the collapsed-pair counts before and after renaming agree (collapsedCount_rename). Collapse also transports across a full two-bijection regime isomorphism (collapsed_transport) and under the combined datum-and-form action (collapsed_renameDataForm). Requirements never enter collapse, so the renaming action leaves them alone.
nodes.bottleneck: The count transport acts on datum indices with forms fixed and takes the pair list and decider as parameters; token renaming is inexpressible in the token-erased Lean model, and the executable count and the identification of the mapped list with the engine's pair enumeration stay computational.

nodes.source_status: genesis_source.txt section 8.4 [finite computation] (CL-BRANCH-REPORTS, CL-TREE-MU2-COMPLETE)
nodes.statement: With the external continuation policy enabled, isomorphism-quotiented branch DAGs were exported for both readings and both measures within the declared bounds. Under mu2 there is no guard cutoff: the quotient tree to the requested 15 transition steps is finite and enumerated in full, 963 nodes for L and 1847 for F, conditional on the orbit policy losing no child classes, and its leaves are round-cut, carrying 10 or 11 separation responses in L and 10, 11 or 12 in F. Under mu1 the 1200-node pre-expansion guard cuts first at depth 6 (L) and 5 (F), leaving exact exported frontiers of 927 and 886 guard-cut nodes. Counted over accepted edges (L mu1, L mu2, F mu1, F mu2), the recurring roles are supply (195/111/233/413), discrimination by one new instance (1047/858/1001/1458), innovation by a fresh form plus instance (8/53/10/83) and double discrimination (6, F mu2 only); the auxiliary-witness shape never appears among accepted minima.

nodes.bottleneck: Reaching the requested depth is not unboundedness and no unboundedness claim is made; mu2 completeness is conditional on CL-TREE-MU2-COMPLETE, the mu1 trees are guard-bounded, and behaviour past the exported depths is unresolved.

nodes.source_status: paper.md section 8 written consequence (ledger WDP-P000-016); companion Paper.lean policy_terminal_separates
nodes.statement: Call a regime a policy terminal when no unseparated admitted pair i < j has a valid response. The companion theorem policy_terminal_separates shows that a well-formed policy terminal whose imposed requirements are all separated separates every admitted pair: an unresolved pair would have the fresh-mark response of mark_progress, contradicting terminality. Together with the round bound, an unguarded maximal run of the declared closure policy cannot continue indefinitely and cannot stop on an unresolved pair for lack of a response.
nodes.bottleneck: The proof goes by contradiction and its axiom report lists Classical.choice; a bounded implementation can instead stop at a search or resource limit, which is not the all-pairs-separated result.

nodes.statement: Section 11 of the sealed manuscript states the terminal result within the declared metatheory and candidate grammar, with one tag per clause. nodes.source_status: paper.md section 9 (ledger WDP-P000-010); PrimDiff.lean D2_initial_pointed
nodes.statement: Let D₂ have carrier {0, 1} and the single edge 0 → 1. For any relation R with a supplied witness R(a, b), the map f(0) = a, f(1) = b preserves the edge, and every map sending 0 to a and 1 to b equals it, so f is the unique endpoint-preserving map from D₂ (D2_initial_pointed). Under irreflexivity this map is injective, because the endpoints of an irreflexive witnessed edge differ (irrefl_witness_ne).
nodes.bottleneck: This represents the chosen witness only: the map need not describe every edge of R or preserve non-edges, needs no reverse edge or composition law, and does not force irreflexivity from opaque marks.

nodes.source_status: paper.md section 10 (ledger WDP-P000-020); QuotientRetention.lean
nodes.statement: Let fine and coarse be equivalence relations on one set with every fine identification also a coarse one. The map [x]_fine ↦ [x]_coarse is well defined and surjective (collapseMap_surjective), injective exactly when every coarse identification also holds finely (collapseMap_injective_iff_reverse_refinement), and successive such maps compose without choosing representatives (collapseMap_compose). If a former identification fails in the finer relation, two distinct fine classes remain over one coarse class (failed_identification_retains_two_classes).

nodes.source_status: paper.md section 10 (ledger WDP-P000-021); PresentationDescent.lean
nodes.statement: For supplied translations f : P → Q and g : Q → P, injective maps i : P → C and j : Q → C with i = j ∘ f and j = i ∘ g exist if and only if g ∘ f = id_P and f ∘ g = id_Q (faithful_descent_iff_round_trip_coherent). One direction substitutes the identifying equations and cancels the injective maps (faithful_descent_to_coherent); the other takes C = P, i = id and j = g. A failed round trip for this declared pair therefore excludes a faithful common carrier that eliminates the presentation index.
nodes.bottleneck: Failure concerns the declared translation pair only: another pair of translations may still close, and no common world prior to P and Q is assumed.

nodes.source_status: paper.md section 10 canonicalization (ledger WDP-P000-022); CanonicalMinimizer.lean and companion PaperCanonical, PaperWire, PaperSearch .lean
nodes.statement: If a representative map C lies in each regime's isomorphism orbit and is constant on orbits, then C(R) = C(S) exactly when R ≅ S, and an injective serialization of the representatives gives the same criterion for keys (key_classification, conditional on both hypotheses). Companion results remove those hypotheses for the concrete search: equal sorted five-field tuples after relabeling by supplied bijections imply isomorphism (serializedRelabel_sound), and the length-prefixed unsigned 64-bit wire encoding is injective on words below 2^64 (portableBytes_injective). Exhaustive search over all datum and form permutations attains a least structural key (canonicalKey_attained), and for well-formed regimes with duplicate-free collections the keys, and under the word bounds their byte encodings, are equal exactly when the regimes are isomorphic (canonicalKey_classification, canonicalBytes_classification).
nodes.bottleneck: The abstract key_classification needs an in-orbit, orbit-invariant choice; the concrete search results assume no orbit oracle but cover the Lean search only, and refinement of the optimized Python and Rust programs remains a separate engineering obligation, checked by finite agreement on 1,436 labelled regimes.

The circulation I(x) = x_ab + x_bc + x_ca vanishes on every d₀g and I(x) = 1, so no integer or rational potential realizes all three records; conversely I(x) = 0 gives the potential (0, x_ab, x_ab + x_bc), so im d₀ = ker I and C¹/im d₀ ≅ ℤ. nodes.source_status: 002_oesn levels/level_20 (E20 written finite example); curriculum.md Lesson 8
nodes.statement: Example E20 works over V = ℚ³ with B = im d₀ = ker I. For linear Q: V → W with K = ker Q, the induced map V/B → W/Q(B) has kernel (B + K)/B ≅ K/(K ∩ B), so quotient observation is injective exactly when K ⊆ B. The defective observer Q_bad(x) = x₁ hides z = (0,1,0), which has Q_bad(z) = 0 and I(z) = 1. Adding the coordinate I(x) gives Q_complete(x) = (x₁, I(x)) with kernel {(0,t,−t)} ⊆ B; the hidden part K/(K ∩ B) has dimension 1 while ker Q_bad has dimension 2, so one added linear functional is necessary and sufficient, and the first projection recovers x₁.

Adjoining two free degree-two generators with the same boundary z₁ gives rank ∂₂ = 1 and dim H₁ = 1, so the receipt count is 2 while the repair rank is 1. Transport from orientation ca to the common basis edge ac needs e_ca = −e_ac, and a wrong sign gives ∂₁z ≠ 0.

WDP-CH04-P06: if Φ₁ > 0 then 0 ≤ R_cl ≤ ‖d₁‖_{J→1}, and the normalized ratio is undefined (0/0) when d₁ = 0. The norm hypothesis (ℝ, ℂ, or ℚ with J restricted from a norm on the real extension) is needed: J(x) = |x₀₁ + √2 x₁₂ + √3 x₀₂| is a norm on ℚ³, yet on the filled triangle with δ = (1, 1, 0) its repair values accumulate at 0, so Φ₁ = 0 while Γ₂ = 2.

The converse needs more than weak connectedness: a base vertex reaching every vertex with path-independent sums, or vanishing periods under signed walks; the difference of two path sums with common endpoints is a period witness, and a nonzero period refutes exactness.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-C4 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status DEFINITION
nodes.statement: If the declared matrices have d1 d0 nonzero mod 2 (or a residual of the wrong length is supplied), the evaluator emits RepresentationInvalid and assigns no residual class.
nodes.bottleneck: The refusal is a rule of the procedure; the Lean lemma only records that a violating vector falsifies the nilpotency predicate.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-EX-TORUS-2X2 claims PROVED_PROSE; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED
nodes.statement: On the 2x2 periodic grid (V = 4, E = 8, F = 4) rank d0 = rank d1 = 3 and dim H1 = 2; the two declared logical cycles are ClosedResidual, a single edge is OpenObstruction, and a d0 column is Exact.
nodes.bottleneck: Fixed instance only; it does not establish the classification on other grids.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-C11 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED
nodes.statement: On the 2x2 torus the logical cycle torus_logical_x has d1 w = 0 on every plaquette yet classifies ClosedResidual (not Exact); on the triangle an exact residual and an open residual are not LGGR.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-THM-SYNDROME-RECOVERY claims PROVED_PROSE; audited status PROVED_PROSE
nodes.statement: For B = im d0, Q = d1 and an admitted error set E in C1, a syndrome-only recovery succeeds for every e in E if and only if (E + E) intersected with ker Q is contained in B.
imported_structure: recovery model: deterministic syndrome-only decoder applying a C1 correction; success means the residual error lies in B
nodes.bottleneck: Lean or exact-code witness of the criterion is absent; the recovery model (deterministic decoder seeing only Qe, success meaning the residual lies in B) is declared in the proof.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-COR-DISTANCE-WEIGHT claims PROVED_PROSE; audited status OPEN
nodes.statement: With d = min{wt(z) : z in ker Q minus B}, the weight-bounded set E_t = {e : wt(e) <= t} satisfies the recovery criterion if and only if 2t < d.
imported_structure: Knill-Laflamme conditions P Ea^dagger Eb P = c_ab P (cited for general channels)
nodes.bottleneck: Write the two-direction weight argument from Theorem 4.4 (sum of two weight-t errors has weight at most 2t; a weight-d logical splits into two weight-at-most-t halves when d <= 2t); the Knill-Laflamme correspondence is cited, not derived.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-OPEN-LOCALITY-VIABILITY claims OPEN; audited status OPEN
nodes.statement: Which distinctions a local system can detect, preserve or repair within a specified time may admit a Lieb-Robinson quantitative extension supporting conditional statements on quantum computing viability.
nodes.bottleneck: No such bound is stated or derived; the source says the papers do not yet justify a general verdict.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-C5 claims DEFINITION; audited status DEFINITION
nodes.statement: Multi-plaquette surface-code models and the FTQC dictionary (error to residual, correctable to Exact, logical to ClosedResidual, detectable to OpenObstruction, distance to declared distance) are diagnostic software schedules, not physical noise processes, threshold certificates or fault-tolerance proofs.
nodes.bottleneck: Any threshold or fault-tolerance theorem for a physical device remains outside this record.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-DEF-TETRON-CARRIER claims DEFINITION; audited status DEFINITION
nodes.statement: A rows x cols tetron array takes MZM sites as vertices on a (rows or rows+1) x (cols or cols+1) grid, nearest-neighbour channels as edges and the rows x cols islands as 2-cells, with no wrap (disk), column wrap (cylinder) or both wraps (torus).
nodes.bottleneck: A tetron here is a 2-cell of a declared combinatorial carrier under an idealized corner-shared layout, not a superconducting island.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-COMP-TETRON-BETTI claims COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED
nodes.statement: For sizes 2x2, 2x3, 3x3, 3x4, 4x4, 5x5, 6x6, 6x8 and 8x8, F2 row reduction gives dim H1 = (E - rank d1) - rank d0 = 0 (disk), 1 (cylinder), 2 (torus), agreeing with (2 if closed else 1) minus the Euler characteristic, with d1 d0 = 0.
nodes.bottleneck: Fixed sizes only; a closed-form proof for all rows and cols is absent.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-LEMMA-TRIVIAL-H1 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-C14 claims COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED
nodes.statement: On the 3x4 tetron torus (12 sites, 24 channels, 12 islands) exhaustive Gray-code coset search gives Phi1 = 3 for the column class, 4 for the row class and 7 for their sum, all ClosedResidual, so the distance of that instance is 3.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-IMPORT-BMVT claims IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION; audited status IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION
nodes.statement: Minimum-weight coset decoding of a binary linear code given by its matrix is NP-hard (Berlekamp, McEliece and van Tilborg 1978).

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-COMP-BUDGET-CAP claims COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED
nodes.statement: When 2^rank(d0) exceeds the declared budget the Gray-code search stops, returns the lightest weight found with exact = False, and the Rust terminal drops from TypedHarmonic to ClosedResidual; checked on the 3x4 torus (budget 4, capped weight >= exact weight) and the 4x4 torus (budget 16).
